Article Title: CDSCO flags 2 Pakistani creams over excess heavy metals
Article Text:
Drug regulator alerts on unauthorised Pakistani whitening creams sale in India. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has warned consumers against using two imported cosmetic creams after testing found them to be unauthorised for sale in India and containing excessive levels of heavy metals that may pose health risks.The cosmetics division of CDSCO has named Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as “Made in Pakistan”, in a public health alert dated September 8. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.CDSCO said laboratory testing and analysis had verified that the products were unauthorised and contained heavy metals beyond specified limits, which could cause toxic effects.The regulator has advised consumers not to buy or use the two products, or similarly named products if already purchased. It has also asked sellers, distributors and other establishments not to sell, distribute or advertise them. Regulatory enforcement units have been directed to ensure that the products are not sold in their jurisdictions.CDSCO said consumers should buy only authorised cosmetics carrying details such as the manufacturing licence number, manufacturer’s details, batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, and, in the case of imported cosmetics, the registration number.The alert comes under the regulatory framework of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Cosmetics Rules, 2020. CDSCO said cosmetic manufacturing for sale requires a licence from the State Licensing Authority, while imported cosmetics must be registered with the Central Licensing Authority.
Article Summary: Drug regulator alerts on unauthorised pakistani whitening creams sale in india. Goree beauty cream and chandni whitening cream, both labelled as “made in pakistan”, in a public health alert dated september 8. Neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale.

NEW DELHI: The AIADMK on Monday took a swipe at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his visit to London to attract investment, questioning the need for such an overseas trip at taxpayers’ expense.The party pointed out that a company established in India in 1986 and headquartered in Noida was among the businesses involved, raising questions over the rationale for Vijay travelling to the UK for investment promotion."A company established in India on 1986 , HQ Noida @actorvijay travels all the way to UK at tax payers money to attract investment," AIADMK spokesperson Kovai Sathyan said in a post on X.Meanwhile, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Sunday also took a swipe at Vijay’s UK visit, saying that while the government projected it as an effort to attract investments, photographs from the trip told a different story.Speaking at the engagement ceremony of an AIADMK functionary in Trichy, Palaniswami indirectly referred to photographs of Vijay flagging off a motor race at Silverstone.“It was believed that he was going to bring investments and improve the state’s economy. However, the photographs published in today’s newspapers tell a different story. Decide for yourself what they represent,” he said.This comes as, Vijay on Monday highlighted a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed in London between Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd and Guidance, Tamil Nadu, for an investment of approximately Rs 11,000 crore in the state."Today (14.09.2026), in London, England, Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd., along with its European and UK-based joint venture companies, entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with Guidance, Tamil Nadu, for an investment of approximately Rs.11,000 crore in Tamil Nadu. Article Title: DRDO has developed indigenous GaN tech for next-gen radars, electronic warfare: Def min report
Article Text:
Meena Mishra, director of DRDO’s Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) led her team that is behind the successful development of indigenous GaN MMIC technology.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO ) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (GaN MMIC) Technology for high-frequency defence systems that can support next-generation radars and electronic warfare systems, the defence ministry's latest annual report for 2025-26 has revealed.After working for years, DRDO developed the GaN MMIC technology in 2024 and helped India quietly entered an elite club of seven countries — US, Russia, France, Germany, South Korea, China — after the country was reportedly denied the technology by a western nation during the negotiations for a major fighter jet deal.In layman’s language, a GaN MMIC is a tiny, super-powerful computer chip built on a special chemical material that handles extremely high-frequency wireless signals without melting. It’s an all-in-one chip that combines tiny parts—like transistors, resistors, and capacitors—onto a single piece of material to manage invisible wireless waves (microwaves).“DRDO has worked on cutting-edge defence technology and it has now matured,” a defence source told TOI. GaN is a material with exceptional thermal and electrical properties, making it critical for advanced defence applications such as sensors, radars, satellites, and missiles.“A single indigenous GaN chip, measuring 3.5 x 3 mm can deliver up to 30 watts of power and operate at speeds 300 times faster than silicon. Indigenous GaN MMIC technology for application upto X band has been successfully demonstrated and implemented,” the ministry’s report said.“Indigenously fabricated S-band GaN High Electron-Mobility power bars, power amplifier, low noise amplifier and switch MMICs have been designed, fabricated and demonstrated,” the report added.Meena Mishra, director of DRDO’s Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) led her team that is behind the successful development of indigenous GaN MMIC technology. Over the course of more than 34 years, Meena has made significant contributions to semiconductor research and has been instrumental in the indigenous development of GaAs and GaN-based MMIC technologies for strategic applications. Her research expertise spans GaAs MESFET-based MMICs, GaAs-based digital integrated circuits, and the modeling, characterisation, and design of high-frequency devices using GaAs and GaN technologies.With rising demands for lighter and more compact power supplies in future combat systems, GaN/SiC technology provides a vital foundation for communications, intelligence, reconnaissance, and unmanned systems for both military and commercial sectors, including electric vehicles and renewable energy.
Article Summary: Defence research and development organisation ( drdo) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous gallium nitride monolithic microwave integrated circuit (gan mmic) technology for high-frequency defence systems. Meena mishra, director of drdo’s solid state physics laboratory (sspl) led her team that is behind the successful development of indigenous ganmmic technology.

Article Title: 'Once again surrendering to US pressure': Rahul slams govt over UPI fee exemption limit
Article Text:
UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 to remain free of charge.

What does the notification say?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul on Tuesday accused the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government of “surrendering to pressure from American corporations” by reportedly paving the way for charges on certain Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions.Rahul argued that although the government has said consumers will not be charged directly, allowing a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 could eventually lead to higher retail prices.Sharing a post on X, the leader of opposition said, "The Modi government has quietly opened the door to imposing fees on UPI. Now, MDR can be levied on merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. Even if these transactions account for just 5% of the volume, they make up nearly 65% of UPI's total transaction value.""The government says no fees will be charged to customers. But where will the fees imposed on shopkeepers ultimately come from? Added to prices, straight out of the customer's pocket. American payment companies have long opposed India's zero-MDR policy. Now, the Modi government has opened the path to changing the policy in exactly that direction. Just like with the US Trade Deal, Compromised PM Modi is once again surrendering to American pressure," he added.Rahul’s remarks came after the government directed banks and payment system providersnot to impose direct or indirect charges on UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000or on payments made through RuPay debit cards.However, the notification does not clarify whether charges could be imposed on transactions above Rs 2,000, particularly those made by merchants. UPI transactions have so far remained free of charges, irrespective of the amount.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also accused the PM Modi government of laying the groundwork for a “Digital Payments Tax” by allowing the possibility of charges on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.“The Modi government's loot has now reached UPI. "No fees on UPI" has been changed to "no fees on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000." Sky-high inflation has already emptied the common man's pocket. Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and the BJP government has planned to impose a "Digital Payments Tax" on the public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left,” Kharge said in an X post.“Ten years ago, demonetization delivered a shock to the country's economy. When questions were raised about the disastrous outcomes of demonetization, the government argued that it was imposed to promote Digital Payments and a Cashless Economy. The Finance Minister had recently stated in Parliament that no Tax or Charges would be levied on UPI, but according to several reports: A potential collection of Rs 25 on a Rs 5,000 transaction and up to Rs 50 on Rs 10,000. Is this true?” he added.He also warned that any Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) imposed on merchants could eventually be passed on to consumers through higher prices.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh also questioned whether the transaction limit could be changed through a future notification to cover person-to-person transfers.“It is evident that the groundwork is being laid to collect fees on UPI transactions from all of us. Tomorrow, through another similar notification, this limit could also be altered—there is now no guarantee of this in the law. As far as we know, the government could impose charges even on everyday person-to-person UPI transactions,” he wrote on X. “Is all this being done with the intent of opening up digital payments for American companies to please President Trump?” he asked.According to a gazette notification dated September 14, no bank or system provider can impose a direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving a payment through a RuPay debit card or a UPI transaction of up to Rs 2,000.The notification follows an amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The amendment provides an enabling framework for imposing MDR on UPI and other notified electronic payment modes.The amendment Bill was passed by Parliament during the Monsoon Session, which concluded on August 13, 2026. The government had said that the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), would decide the MDR rates.The government has argued that rising transaction volumes require continuous investment in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and payment infrastructure. It has also said that charges would support market expansion, encourage competition and help create a self-sustaining revenue model for the payments ecosystem.UPI is operated by NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India and the Indian Banks’ Association. It enables real-time payments between individuals and allows customers to pay merchants directly.Launched on August 25, 2016, UPI has transformed India’s digital payments landscape. Its transaction value rose from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26, an increase of more than 4,000 times in a decade.UPI is now accepted in 11 countries, including Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Greece and Uzbekistan.According to Reuters, the introduction of UPI charges could benefit Paytm and Pine Labs, create an additional revenue stream for banks and improve prospects for IPO-bound PhonePe and Razorpay. Analysts at Jefferies estimate that the fees could generate Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 10,000 crore annually for the payments industry.
Article Summary: Upi transactions of up to rs 2,000 to remain free of charge. Congress leader rahul says allowing a merchant discount rate (mdr) could lead to higher retail prices. Upi transactions have so far remained free of charges irrespective of the amount. The amendment bill was passed by parliament during the monsoon session, which concluded on august 13, 2026.

Article Title: In 2017, Kevin Durant put $250,000 into an AI startup nobody had heard of. It just sold for $12.9 billion and could hand him a bigger payday than any NBA season ever has
Article Text:
Kevin Durant’s $250,000 Hugging Face bet could now be worth more than $60 million after Nvidia’s acquisition

Durant invested $250,000 in Hugging Face before its rise

Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal changed the equation

The potential return is bigger than Durant's annual NBA salary

Boardroom Talks

Hugging Face is only one of Durant's major investments

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kevin Durant has made a fortune from basketball, but one of his more intriguing financial moves came well away from the court. Long before artificial intelligence became one of the biggest investment stories in the world. The Houston Rockets star was putting money into a young technology company years before it became a major player in the open-source AI world. Years later, that decision has put a surprisingly large figure next to what was originally a relatively modest bet.The investment began when Hugging Face was still a relatively young technology company, long before artificial intelligence became such a dominant part of the technology industry. Durant and his longtime business partner Rich Kleiman backed the company through their investment platform, 35V, taking part in two of its early fundraising rounds.According to entrepreneur and sports-business writer Joe Pompliano, Durant invested $100,000 during Hugging Face's seed round before committing another $150,000 in its Series A financing. Together, those investments amounted to $250,000.That was a small commitment compared with the scale of Durant's basketball earnings, but it was made at a particularly early stage of Hugging Face's development.The company would go on to become one of the most widely used platforms for sharing and working with open-source AI models, building a large community around the development and distribution of AI technology.Durant was not hiding his involvement. In 2017, he publicly signalled his backing of the company on social media while promoting a new Hugging Face release.“Excited for the new release of #HuggingFace durant.ly/huggingface - proud investor!” Durant wrote.Nearly a decade later, that early bet has taken on a very different significance following Nvidia's agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion.Pompliano estimates that Durant and Kleiman's investment could now be worth more than $60 million, a figure that would turn the original $250,000 commitment into an extraordinary return.“He likely made more than $60 million in this investment alone,” Pompliano wrote, calling it “one of the best athlete investments ever.”The size of that potential return should nevertheless be treated carefully. Durant's exact ownership stake in Hugging Face has not been made public, so the $60 million figure is an estimate rather than a confirmed payout. The final amount he could receive will depend on the stake he actually holds and the terms and structure of Nvidia's acquisition.Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion, with the deal officially announced on September 3, 2026.According to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Hugging Face chief executive Clement Delangue, the AI company's team approached Nvidia during the summer as it looked to expand its computing resources.Hugging Face is expected to continue operating as an open platform for the global AI community following the acquisition.For Durant, the timing turns an early venture bet into a potentially extraordinary paper return. Pompliano's estimate would represent roughly a 23,900% return on the original $250,000 investment.It would also put the potential windfall above Durant's biggest single-season NBA salary.Durant is entering his 19th NBA season and is scheduled to earn $43.9 million with the Houston Rockets during the 2026-27 season, according to Spotrac.His contract is a two-year, $90 million deal, with a $46.1 million player option for 2027-28.Even after 18 NBA seasons, Durant has never earned $60 million in salary in a single season. His highest salary to date was $53.3 million last season, according to Spotrac.Across his NBA career, Durant has accumulated $501.1 million in earnings, according to Bleacher Report.That makes the estimated Hugging Face return unusual even by the standards of one of the NBA's highest-paid players: a reported investment of $250,000 could potentially produce more than he has ever earned from the NBA in one season.Durant has also spoken openly about the possibility of retirement, particularly after former teammate Russell Westbrook announced his own retirement.During an episode of, Durant said:“I'm on deck,” he said. “... It's a young man's game. Even though I still feel like I can play, I always hear, 'you're 38, you're 39. You're getting up there.' I get that. But I put everything into the game, and I'm cool with whatever happens moving forward. I'm going to continue putting everything into the game until I can't.”At 38, Durant's investment activity has therefore become an increasingly significant part of his business career away from basketball.The potential Hugging Face windfall is not Durant and Kleiman's only notable investment success.Through 35V and other investment vehicles, the pair have built a portfolio spanning technology, finance, consumer businesses, sports and other sectors.Among their investments are companies including Robinhood and Coinbase, both of which have since gone public.The portfolio also includes Acorns, Dapper Labs, Kalshi, Spindrift and Whoop, alongside stakes in the Philadelphia Union of Major League Soccer and Paris Saint-Germain.The Hugging Face investment nevertheless stands apart because of the size of the reported return relative to the original commitment.For now, the final number remains dependent on Durant's undisclosed stake and the completion and structure of Nvidia's acquisition. The $60 million-plus figure is Pompliano's estimate, not a confirmed payment to Durant.
Article Summary: Kevin durant invested $250,000 in hugging face before its rise as an open-source ai platform. Nvidia has agreed to acquire the company for approximately $12.9 billion. Durant's investment could now be worth more than $60 million. The potential return is bigger than his annual nba salary.

Article Title: L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes $5.1 million hit on futuristic mansion after listing it for $32.5 million and making multiple price cuts
Article Text:
L.A. Olympics chairman Casey Wasserman takes major mansion loss. Image via: Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images | Realtor.com

Casey Wasserman sells futuristic mansion at a major loss

Inside the Bird Streets estate that inspired the loss

The infinity pool of Casey Wasserman's former LA mansion. Image via: Realtor.com

Did Casey Wasserman's controversy impact the sale?

Casey Wasserman had another financial hit involving his talent agency

Casey Wasserman closed the door on his futuristic Hollywood Hills home. The numbers, however, were not what he expected. The chairman of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics sold his award-winning Bird Streets estate for $18.5 million, a steep comedown from the $32.5 million he originally asked for it.The sale caps months of markdowns on a house once celebrated for its design. It also lands at an odd moment for the 52-year-old sports and entertainment mogul, whose name has been tied to headlines that have nothing to do with real estate.Casey Wasserman listed the property in September 2025, five years after it won the AIA Los Angeles Award for the city's most influential architecture. Buyers weren't rushing in. By February, he had shaved $2.6 million off the price, dropping it to $29.9 million. Still, it wasn't enough, so the number fell again, this time to $24.9 million.Realtor.com reports the home eventually sold for $18.5 million. Wasserman had paid $23.6 million for it back in August 2020, which puts his loss on the deal at roughly $5.1 million. It was a heavy hit.The house sits on what the listing calls the most prime cul-de-sac in Bird Streets, one of the most exclusive pockets of the Hollywood Hills. Designed by XTEN Architects, the place draws heavily from Stanley Kubrick's "2001: A Space Odyssey," right down to ceilings that reportedly cost more than $1 million to build.Five bedrooms and seven bathrooms fill roughly 12,000 square feet, and the primary suite leans into a dark, moody look with glass walls that pull in light and sweeping views. A wall installation inside reads "More, Faster, Now," while an eight-car underground garage sits below a home that also includes a private theater, a dance studio, and an infinity pool overlooking the hillside.It's a far cry from the last mansion Wasserman parted with. In June 2020, he sold his custom Beverly Hills estate, the Foothill Estate, to music executive David Geffen for $68 million. That home was built where his grandfather, the late entertainment titan Lew Wasserman, once lived, and it had originally been listed for $125 million.The sale comes months after Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass publicly called for Wasserman to step down as LA28 chairman. Her reasoning traced back to emails between Wasserman and Ghislaine Maxwell that surfaced in Department of Justice files released in February 2026. Bass didn't hold back when asked about it, telling CNN, "My opinion is that he should step down."Wasserman has said his contact with Maxwell and Jeffrey Epstein amounted to one humanitarian trip to Africa in 2002 and a handful of emails he now regrets. The LA28 board's executive committee reviewed the matter and sided with him, stating that his relationship with the pair "did not go beyond what has already been publicly documented." He kept his post.Whether the controversy nudged buyers away from the mansion is impossible to say for certain. But the timing, arriving in the same stretch as the price cuts, hasn't gone unnoticed.The house wasn't the only asset Wasserman put up for sale this year. Days after the LA28 committee finished its review, he told staff at his talent agency, Wasserman, that he had begun selling the company. In his memo, he wrote that he had become a distraction to its work and said Mike Watts would take over daily operations while he focused on the Olympics.The fallout from the Maxwell emails had already cost the agency clients. Chappell Roan, Odesza, Orville Peck, and retired soccer star Abby Wambach all cut ties. By July 2026, the agency was working toward a buyout of Wasserman's stake backed by Providence Equity Partners, with Watts stepping in as CEO and Providence taking majority ownership.
Article Summary: L.a. olympics chairman casey wasserman takes major mansion loss. Wasserman had paid $23.6 million for it back in august 2020, which puts his loss on the deal at roughly $5.1 million. The sale comes months after los angeles mayor karen bass publicly called for wasserman to step down as la28 chairman.

Article Title: Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon: Report
Article Text:
Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon

Why Meta glasses are facing privacy concerns

Luna could focus on Meta AI instead of recording

Meta has already tried to stop hidden recording

Developers are building tools to detect smart glasses

Meta expands its AI subscription business

Meta is reportedly working on a new pair of smart glasses without a camera, a major change from its existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup. The reported move comes as camera-equipped smart glasses face growing privacy concerns and bans in places such as schools and cinemas. The new glasses, reportedly codenamed “Luna,” are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. According to The Information, Meta could unveil the glasses at its developer conference on September 23-24, with shipments expected to begin in October.As per the report, Luna will have six built-in microphones and a side button that can give users quick access to Meta AI. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The speakers are reportedly similar to those used in Meta's current smart glasses.The reported camera-free glasses come as Meta smart glasses face growing privacy concerns. A BBC investigation in January this year identified dozens of accounts that had posted videos of women recorded in public without their consent using Meta glasses. One such video showed the face and phone number of a 21-year-old woman and received more than 1.3 million views.The concerns have also spread to public places. Schools, cinemas and other venues have increasingly banned smart glasses because of the possibility of people being recorded without their knowledge.The reported Luna design suggests Meta may be trying a different approach to AI glasses. The six microphones could make voice interaction the main way users communicate with Meta AI and Muse. The absence of a camera could also make the glasses more acceptable in places where recording devices are not allowed.Meta's existing Ray-Ban Meta glasses have reportedly sold around 7 million units, showing strong interest in AI-powered wearable devices. The challenge for Luna will be whether consumers find voice-based AI useful enough without the camera features that helped make smart glasses attractive.Meta announced a software update in July 2026 aimed at detecting when the recording LED has been “physically tampered with or destroyed.” The company said it would block camera recording when such tampering is detected.Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth has also said the recording light was designed so that people nearby could notice when the camera is being used. However, the privacy debate has continued as more people use camera-equipped smart glasses.Privacy concerns have also led to independent tools designed to identify nearby smart glasses. One example is ZuckOff, a free mobile app developed by Polish developer Pawel Szydlowski. The app uses Bluetooth signals to identify smart glasses that may be nearby.The app can recognise signals associated with devices including Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta and Snap Spectacles. It can provide an approximate idea of how close a pair of glasses is, although it cannot tell whether the glasses are actively recording or identify the person wearing them.The reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services. On September 15, Meta announced Meta One, a subscription service offering additional AI features across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. The company said the service has already reached 15 million subscriptions and trials during its phased rollout. Meta plans to expand the service to Edits and AI glasses.
Article Summary: New glasses, reportedly codenamed ‘luna,’ are expected to focus on voice-based ai instead of photo and video recording. Luna will have six built-in microphones and a side button that can give users quick access to meta ai. The glasses are also expected to support meta's new consumer ai agent, muse.

Article Title: HBO CEO on Apple TV, which has been called 'the new HBO' by some, winning the most number of Emmy awards; and beating Netflix and Amazon
Article Text:
HBO at Emmys over the years

Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The iPhone-makers' Apple TV proved to be the most successful studio at the Emmys 2026. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total, including six “Pluribus” wins, three for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles,” three for “Palm Royale,” one for “Slow Horses” and one for “Mr. Scorsese.” This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.Interestingly, Apple TV has long been compared to HBO. In fact, Apple has even been called "the new HBO" at times by some analysts. HBO boss Casey Bloys was asked by Deadline after the awards show for his reaction to Apple’s performance. In an interview conducted during HBO Max’s afterparty at the San Vicente Bungalows, Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, spoke about the company’s Emmy win. Bloys was asked what he thinks about Apple TV’s performance and their first time finishing as the No. 1 platform at the Emmys?' To this, HBO CEO replied, "Well, I’m very happy because I think that they’re very handsome competitors, Zack and Jamie. Look, we’ve had very formidable competitors in going back to Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon, so [when] Apple, everybody, keeps us on our toes, I think we do our best work.It’s a little scary that they’re a trillion-dollar company, but we’ll continue to do what we do, which is put out the best shows that we can."Reacting to the wins, former Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote on Twitter, "Stories have the power to move us, inspire us, and bring us closer together. Congrats to the Apple TV creators, cast, and crews behind the incredible work celebrated at the Emmys for Widow’s Bay, Pluribus, Slow Horses, Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Palm Royale, and Mr. Scorsese!"HBO was first allowed entry into the Emmys in the year 1988. The studio has been a dominant force at the Emmys ever since, initially competing with the broadcast networks, then basic and premium cable networks and, most recently, streamers like Netflix, Apple TV and Amazon’s Prime Video.In 2026, HBO shared the No. 1 title with Netflix for most Emmy wins. This year, it finished second to Apple TV with 21 wins versus Apple's 28. HBO won Outstanding Drama Series for 'The Pitt' and Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series with DTF St. Louis. After HBO Max, at the No. 3 was Netflix. The American streaming giant got 16 wins. Netflix winners include “Beef,” “Love on the Spectrum,” “Bridgerton,” “The Beast in Me” and more.

Article Title: Person-to-merchant UPI payments over Rs 2,000 to attract MDR : What remains free, what will come under MDR and other things to know
Article Text:
Person-to-merchant UPI payments over Rs 2,000 to attract MDR : What remains free, what will come under MDR and other things to know

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: What will remain free

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: What will attract MDR

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Customers will not pay MDR

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Most merchant transactions will remain unaffected

When do the updated MDR provisions take effect

Will small-value UPI transactions be impacted

Will UPI apps start charging platform fee on UPI payments

Will I need to pay a fee when scanning a QR code at a local vendor

Do small merchants need to upgrade or change their existing QR codes

What happens if a small merchant receives a payment above Rs 2,000

UPI AutoPay: No prescribed MDR charges

The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced a 0.4% fee on person-to-merchant transactions exceeding Rs 2,000. Called Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), it is a charge that a merchant pays to a bank or payment service provider for processing a digital payment. Introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the new MDR provision will come into effect from October 15, 2026. In an official press release, the government clarified that the new UPI framework will have “no impact on any person to person transactions”. “UPI will continue to remain completely free for all person-to-person transactions, irrespective of the amount transferred,” the release said. Instead, “the framework seeks to ensure the long-term sustainability of UPI while protecting individuals and small merchants from additional charges,” it stated.With the new framework coming into force next month, here’s what the government said about what UPI payments remain free, what has been included under the MDR provisions and whether UPI apps will start charging platform fees on UPI payments.All Person-to-Person Transactions: All person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will remain completely free, irrespective of the amount transferred.No transaction fee, platform fee or other charge may be imposed on individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI. Therefore, UPI transactions accounting for 70% of the total transaction value will remain completely outside the MDR framework.Merchant Payments Up to Rs 2,000: All person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions up to Rs 2,000 will remain free of MDR. Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI.Payments Received by Small Merchants: Small merchants including street vendors receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to enjoy zero MDR on all transactions. This provision will protect street vendors, neighbourhood shops and other small businesses from additional payment costs.Merchant Transactions Above Rs 2,000: A nominal MDR of 0.4% will apply only to P2M transactions above Rs 2,000. The MDR will be shared among payment ecosystem participants, including banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers. For transactions of Rs 75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction.Transactions in Essential Sectors: Transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential and thin-margin sectors, including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5 per transaction. The flat charge will provide cost certainty for critical public services and businesses operating on narrow margins.Capital Market Transactions: Payments relating to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction. The lower rate is intended to support continued retail participation in formal financial markets.MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments. In its official announcement, the government said that banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges.Individuals will continue to have unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions. Daily transaction limits prescribed by banks and NPCI, generally ranging from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh depending on the transaction category, are security and risk-management safeguards. They are not charging thresholds.Data analysis indicates that MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions. This means that approximately 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected, as they are either below the Rs 2,000 threshold or covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants.The framework therefore protects individuals, micro-enterprises and small businesses while introducing a limited charge on larger merchant transactions.The finalized MDR framework and threshold structure take effect from 15th October 2026. This timeline gives acquiring banks, payment aggregators, fintech applications, and corporate accounting platforms adequate lead time to update their software engines and billing systems.There is no impact on small-value UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000, which comprise more than 95% of the total volume of UPI (P2M) transactions. The intent of levying reasonable MDR is to ensure that UPI remains, accessible and convenient for everyday transactions while supporting long-term ecosystem sustainability.No, UPI App providers shall NOT charge Platform Fee or any other charge for any payment made through UPI. UPI applications are explicitly restricted from levying platform fees on UPI transactions.No, scanning QR codes at local markets, street vendors, or small retail shops will remain completely free for consumers. The customer-facing side of a QR transaction involves zero fees, regardless of the purchase amount. The policy has been engineered to protect daily micro-purchases like tea stalls, and local transport from any cost burden. Consumers can continue scanning QR codes with total confidence that no extra charge will be deducted.No. Existing QR infrastructure will continue to function normally. Merchants do not need to replace, re-register, or alter their existing physical QR stands or soundboxes. All UPI QR codes currently displayed across shops will continue to process payments without interruption. Merchants can receive customer payments through their existing setups without visiting a bank branch or updating software.MDR applicability is determined by overall merchant account categorisation. Receiving a payment above Rs 2,000 does not impose a charge on a small merchant operating under exempted tiers like P2PM. A MDR of 0.4% will be introduced on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000/-. For transactions of Rs 75,000/- and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction.The government says that recurring payments made through UPI Mandates or AutoPay—such as utility bills, OTT subscriptions and mutual fund subscriptions—do not carry prescribed MDR transaction charges. Hence, they will continue to remain free of any fees.
Article Summary: The national payments corporation of india (npci) has introduced a 0.4% fee on person-to-merchant transactions exceeding rs 2,000. Called merchant discount rate (mdr), it is a charge that a merchant pays to a bank or payment service provider for processing a digital payment. The new mdr provision will come into effect from october 15, 2026.

Article Title: Microsoft to host Windows and Surface event on October 7
Article Text:
Microsoft Windows event details

What to expect

Microsoft has confirmed that it will host the on October 7, 2026, in San Francisco. The event will focus on how local AI is shaping the future of personal computing, marking the company’s most significant Windows showcase in over two years. The event is scheduled for 10 AM PT (1 PM ET) and marks Microsoft's first major Windows event since May 2024. Microsoft is framing the event as a conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC. CEO Satya Nadella, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, and Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri are all confirmed to attend, a lineup that strongly hints at what's coming.* Date & Time: October 7, 2026, at 10 AM PT / 1 PM ET* Location: San Francisco, California* Theme: “A conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC”This marks Microsoft’s first major Windows event in over two years, following its May 2024 showcase of Arm-based Copilot Plus PCs and its renewed Qualcomm partnership.The pairing of Microsoft and NVIDIA leadership points toward more details on the Surface Laptop Ultra, which Microsoft unveiled in June 2026 without announcing pricing or availability. The laptop is built around NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform, the company's first system-on-a-chip designed for Windows, and is widely seen as Microsoft's answer to Apple's MacBook Pro. Microsoft has also shown off a Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a compact desktop using the same chip aimed at developers working with local AI models, which could also get more details at the event.Other PC makers, including Dell, Lenovo, and Asus, have already announced their own RTX Spark-based devices, though none have published benchmarks yet, and Microsoft's event could be where pricing and launch timing finally get nailed down across the ecosystem.Despite the "Windows" branding on the invite, a new version of the operating system itself is not expected — Microsoft isn't expected to announce a surprise Windows 12. Instead, the focus looks to be squarely on hardware and on-device AI capability, with Microsoft having spent months tuning Windows 11 specifically for the new RTX Spark hardware.The event caps a year in which Microsoft has been pushing AI agents further into everyday computing, and comes on the heels of its Project Solara device concepts, which have signaled where the company sees Windows hardware heading next.

Article Title: Bill Gates announces $1 billion donation to AI efforts after warning that this technology poses grave threat to jobs and human life
Article Text:
Targeting healthcare, farming and language inclusivity

Bill Gates warns of economic turbulence

The Gates Foundation, founded by Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates, has announced a donation of $1 billion across the next two years to broaden worldwide access to artificial intelligence (AI) and deploy the technology to solve systemic social disparities. The massive funding pledge, revealed in the organisation’s yearly Goalkeepers report, arrives alongside urgent warnings from foundation chairman and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, who has cautioned that unchecked AI models pose severe threat to human life and global employment stability.The initiative aims to redirect computational breakthroughs toward underserved populations, with the report emphasising that immediate intervention is needed to ensure machine learning closes societal divides rather than widening them.The capital will be distributed among outside organisations working across the foundation's core social focus areas. Key sectors that the foundation will fund include initiatives that integrate automated tools into routine clinical healthcare, classroom instruction and agricultural practices. Grants will back the creation of localised data repositories across a wider variety of global dialects. The report (via The New York Times) highlighted that early frontier models were trained overwhelmingly on English text, effectively locking out vulnerable communities from the data foundations powering modern software.Without deliberate intervention, the foundation cautioned, cutting-edge software will be tailored exclusively to commercial entities with the deepest pockets, entirely bypassing those who stand to gain the most. The report stressed that society has only a narrow window to alter who benefits from this transformation.Gates has grown increasingly vocal regarding the damage of rapid automation. Writing on his personal blog last month, the billionaire predicted that the technological shift may become one of the most chaotic eras in human history, adding that the technology will either serve as humanity's greatest equalizer or its most destructive source of injustice.Gates warned that the rapid integration of intelligent software across commercial sectors risks triggering widespread workforce displacement. As multiple fields are automating simultaneously, displaced laborers may find few alternative industries capable of taking them in.He also accused tech developers of soft-pedaling real-world risks, arguing that tech corporations remain quiet because massive financial fortunes are on the line as giants race to market worker-replacing software to corporate clients.
Article Summary: The gates foundation has pledged $1 billion over the next two years. The money will be used to expand worldwide access to artificial intelligence. The initiative aims to redirect computational breakthroughs toward underserved populations. Bill gates has warned that unchecked ai models pose a threat to human life.

Article Title: Apple rolls out its biggest iPhone software update of 2026: 10 ways iOS 27 will 'change' your iPhone
Article Text:
Apple's iOS 27 is out for iPhone 11 and newer, with Siri AI as the headline change.

iOS 27 compatible iPhones: the list stretches back to 2019

iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max

The complete iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 lines, including the 16e and 17e

iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo

iPhone SE, second generation onward

How to update to iOS 27

Back up first through Settings, your name, iCloud Backup, Back Up Now. Use a computer instead if your iCloud storage has run out.

Open Settings, General, Software Update. Swipe down on the page if iOS 27 is not showing yet.

Select iOS 27 and follow the prompts. A number of users have watched the installer describe itself as 26.7 before the phone reboots onto iOS 27.

Switch Siri AI on afterwards in Settings. It stays off until you ask for it, and it is not available to anyone under 13.

Siri AI knows what is in your inbox, and answers from it

Finding a mail, message, photo, link or file by person, date or place

Building a home automation from an instruction such as locking every door at midnight

Adding a birthday or a second number to a contact without opening the app

Lifting every ingredient off a recipe page into a shopping list

Answering questions about whatever is on screen, and searching the web when it has to

Point the camera at a restaurant bill and Siri splits it

Write with Siri copies your tone before it writes a word

Older iPhones feel quicker, and Liquid Glass gets a dial

Shortcuts builds the automation from one sentence

Photos can extend a shot past the edges of the frame

Safari watches a product page and tells you when the price falls

AirPods finally get a custom EQ, alarms get their own volume

A child now has to ask before opening a new website

Ask to Buy holds every app install until a parent says yes

Ask to Browse does the same for new websites in Safari, with the request arriving in the parent's Messages

Communication Safety, which already caught nudity, now intervenes on gore and violence in shared images and video

Time Allowances cap daily use across Entertainment, Games and Social Media, with age guidance Apple developed with clinical and child development specialists, while Schedules decide which apps work at which hours

One phone number across two iPhones, for a monthly fee

The smaller iOS 27 changes are the ones you will stumble into

Save a single frame from a video as a photo, instead of screenshotting and cropping it. Anyone who shoots video of moving children or pets has wanted this for years.

A Captured By Me filter in Photos separates pictures you actually took from the flood of forwards in your library, reaching back across older iPhones.

Wallet builds a pass from a photograph of a physical card, so a library card or a gift voucher stops living in a drawer. There is a manual template route if your iPhone does not support Apple Intelligence.

Home screen widgets stretch to an extra large size, which makes Notes, Calendar and Weather worth reading rather than tapping through. Weather now shows nine days instead of five.

Choose which eight controls sit above the Camera viewfinder. Lens Aperture and Shutter Speed are reserved for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

Messages stops holding up your next text while a large photo crawls out over weak cellular.

Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year, and it is free for every iPhone 11 and newer. The rollout started on Monday and the update is live in India now. The headline is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers. Underneath that sit a Camera app that can read a restaurant bill, a Shortcuts app you can talk into shape, a Photos editor that pushes a picture past its own borders, and a slider for everyone who spent the last year quietly resenting Liquid Glass.Siri AI is also the feature Apple has owed its users since 2024. The personalised, context aware assistant it demonstrated that year never shipped on schedule, and the gap was long enough that a fair number of iPhone owners stopped waiting and installed a chatbot instead. What arrives today is that promise, delivered late and still carrying a beta label, with English first and French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish following in October.Apple has hedged the rest of the release accordingly. A great deal of engineering in iOS 27 has gone into things that have nothing to do with AI, from app launch times to how the phone hands over between Wi-Fi and cellular, which is the part of this update that will reach the most people.iOS 27 installs on:Apple Intelligence and Siri AI need a shorter list: iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model and later, the iPhone Air and the iPhone Duo. A handful of features sit on an even narrower shelf. Tuning how Siri sounds, down to pitch and pace, is restricted to the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Duo, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and Air.The new assistant works like a chatbot with one thing no rival has, which is private access to what is already on the phone. When you install the update it indexes your calendar invites, mail, texts, files and notes, then answers from that. Ask for a recent photo of your dog and it surfaces several. Ask which weekend you were in Goa and it knows, because your boarding passes told it. The working list includes:Say the wake word and a shimmering orb appears in the Dynamic Island with a card you can pull down into a full Siri app, which keeps your conversations and continues them on an iPad. It now asks which part of a request it did not follow rather than failing silently. It is still slower to respond than Gemini, and it fumbles retrievals a well indexed inbox should make easy.Swipe past Photo and Video in the Camera app and a Siri tab appears. Hold it over a nutrition label and the numbers go into Health. Hold it over a shopfront and ask for the hours. Hold it over an event schedule and each entry lands in your calendar. The demo everyone will run is the receipt split, which reads the bill, works out each person's share with tax and tip, and settles the total through Apple Cash. Printed receipts scan reliably. Handwriting is a gamble. The Apple Cash requirement also means this is a feature Indian users can admire and not use.Siri can draft inside any text field, rewrite what you have typed, shift the register, or tell you where a draft is weak. In Messages and Mail it reads your existing writing and imitates your phrasing and punctuation, which is the difference between a useful draft and one you delete. Grammar suggestions now appear alongside spelling corrections across the system.Apple's own testing puts app launches up to 30 per cent faster, newly shot photos loading up to 70 per cent faster in the library, and AirDrop transfers up to 80 per cent faster. Treat the figures as the company's, but the change registers within minutes, and it lands on every supported handset instead of only the Apple Intelligence tier. Messages retries a failed send by itself now, and the switch between Wi-Fi and cellular is less jarring. For the look of the thing, Settings, Appearance, Liquid Glass opens a slider that runs from ultra clear to fully tinted.Shortcuts has always been capable and almost nobody used it, because building anything meant stacking actions by hand and guessing at the logic. Now you tap the plus sign, write what you want, and the app assembles it. Message a family member your ETA when you leave the office, or trigger a playlist when CarPlay connects. You can refine the result in plain language or edit the steps yourself.Clean Up has been the softest of Apple's editing tools since it launched, mostly because it left warped patches behind. It now runs in three modes: Fast, on device, for small removals, High Quality, which goes to Apple's servers, and Auto. Beside it are Extend, which invents what lies past the original frame, and Spatial Reframing, which shifts the apparent camera position after the picture was taken. Image Playground handles photorealistic output now, and Apple has said SynthID watermarking support is coming later this year.Notify Me is the smartest small idea in this release. Find the listing in Safari, open the Tab bar menu, tap Notify Me, describe the change you are waiting for and set how often the browser should check. It watches the page for a restock or a price cut and alerts you. Safari also sorts open tabs into topics on its own, and will write a custom extension from a plain description, from a citation generator to forcing a minimum font size on a site with unreadable type.You can tune the lows, mids and highs on AirPods yourself rather than accepting Apple's preset, through AirPods settings, Audio and Routing, Equaliser, Custom. It works on AirPods 4 and 5, AirPods Pro 2 and 3, and AirPods Max 2. Separately, Settings, Sounds and Haptics lets you unlink alarm volume from ringer volume, which fixes the old problem of sleeping through an alarm or being startled by a notification at maximum volume. GymKit also arrives on iPhone, and AirPods Pro 3 can pass heart rate data into a workout.The parental controls are the most substantial non AI work in this release, and they are built around approval rather than blocking:Screen Time itself has been redesigned around an at a glance view of what a child actually used.Two iPhones running iOS 27 can share a single number, with the line following whichever handset you unlock. It is set up in Settings, Cellular, This iPhone and Another. The obstacle is the carrier. Only T-Mobile supports it at launch, at roughly Rs 440 a month, with Verizon expected later this year and no Indian operator involved yet.Some of the best work in this update never made a slide. These are the fixes that remove a daily irritation rather than add a headline, and most of them land on older iPhones too.The bigger leftovers come with conditions attached. Call Context surfaces a confirmation code or a booking reference from your mail while you are on a call to a business. HomeKit Secure Video cameras record and stream in 4K, and the Home app can describe what happened in a clip or search footage in plain language, although those AI pieces need a 2TB iCloud+ plan for a single camera and more beyond that. Maps Flyover renders architectural detail and individual trees from aerial imagery. Cycle Tracking in Health adds perimenopause support, with deviation notifications aimed at users over 40. iCloud Shared Albums allow full resolution sharing at last, and are easier to join from Android or Windows. VoiceOver and Magnifier both pick up substantial accessibility work.One to wait for rather than look for: the Passwords app will update weak or compromised logins on your behalf, but Apple has marked that as coming in a future release rather than shipping it today.
Article Summary: Apple has released ios 27, the largest iphone software update it has shipped all year. The rollout started on monday and the update is live in india now. The headline change is siri ai, a rebuilt assistant that reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.

While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.

Article Title: Meet Austin Jin, the 16-year-old Great Neck, New York student who built a CRISPR blood test to detect tuberculosis and drug resistance; he won $50,000
Article Text:
Outside the lab, Jin captains his varsity swim team and co-presidents his DECA chapter. He also co-founded Project LIFE, a student-led initiative that has grown to over 20 chapters in eight states, with a mission to improve education and access to the bone marrow registry.

Another approach to TB diagnosis

Drug resistance testing

Research to broader impact

Most teenagers go to a pathology office for a blood test. For Austin Jin, it was the launch pad to address one of medicine’s oldest and most enduring problems: diagnosing tuberculosis. A 16-year-old senior at William A. Shine Great Neck South High School in Great Neck, NY, developed M-CATCH, a diagnostic platform based on CRISPR that can detect tuberculosis from blood and identify drug-resistant strains. According to the Davidson Institute website, his work earned him the 2026 Davidson Fellowship and a $50,000 scholarship. Scroll down to read about his journey.Tuberculosis remains a major global health threat with over a million deaths reported annually worldwide. But one of the biggest challenges in fighting the disease comes even before treatment starts: getting an accurate diagnosis. Sputum, the mucus produced deep in the lungs, is used in many standard TB tests. And that creates a particular problem for young children and severely ill or immunocompromised patients, many of whom have difficulty producing a usable sample.But in the online report, Jin’s project takes a different tack.M-CATCH screens the blood serum for circulating bacterial DNA fragments in the blood. The system uses polymerase chain reactions and CRISPR-Cas12a technology to find genetic signatures associated with tuberculosis.This test is not intended to determine whether tuberculosis exists. It can also look for genetic alterations that make the bacteria resistant to certain drugs and that level of detection can come down to a single change in DNA. Jin engineered CRISPR guide RNAs that can distinguish between these tiny genetic differences and combined them with a microfluidics chip that allows multiple reactions to occur at the same time.The result is a multiplex platform that can screen hundreds of reactions for more than one mutation simultaneously. This could eventually make large-scale testing more practical, especially in places where sophisticated laboratories are not readily available.The path to the finished system had its challenges. Designing good CRISPR guide RNAs was particularly tricky because many candidates that looked good on paper did not work as expected in experiments. Jin had spent weeks testing and tweaking them. He’s interested in more than tuberculosis. He plans to major in biomedical engineering and biochemistry to prepare for a career as a physician-scientist, with the hope of translating laboratory research into useful tools for medicine.Outside the lab, Jin captains his varsity swim team and co-presidents his DECA chapter. He also co-founded Project LIFE, a student-led initiative that has grown to over 20 chapters in eight states, with a mission to improve education and access to the bone marrow registry.His M-CATCH platform could eventually be adapted to detect other infectious diseases and possibly even cancer, suggesting a future where a small blood sample could reveal far more than a single diagnosis.Images Courtesy: Davidson Institute

His work earned him the 2026 davidson fellowship and a $50,000 scholarship. He plans to major in biomedical engineering and biochemistry to prepare for a career as a physician-scientist.

Article Title: In 2011, a man opened his late great-aunt’s Virginia closet and found 345 comics; the collection including Batman comics sold for about $3.5 million
Article Text:
AI Representation: A stack of vintage comic books discovered in a Virginia home in 2011, part of a collection later sold for $3.5 million. Image credits: Chatgpt

Paper quality from that era makes surviving copies unusually fragile

Detective Comics No. 27

led the sale at $522,813

At the 2014 New York Comic Con, Vincent Zurzolo of Metropolis Collectibles displays the CGC 9.0 copy of Action Comics #1. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The total sale brought in about $3.5 million

Michael Rorrer, a 31-year-old Oxnard, California, resident, discovered 345 comics in a basement closet in his late great-aunt's Martinsville, Virginia, home in 2011, a collection quietly assembled decades earlier by his great-uncle Billy Wright. According to the Associated Press, Wright, who died in 1994 at age 66, collected the comics as a boy and young man between 1936 and 1941, later becoming a chemical engineer, and never discussed the collection with relatives beyond one brief mention. Heritage Auctions described the find as one of the most important Golden Age comic book collections in decades. Heritage Auctions reported in February 2012 that 44 of the 345 comics in Wright's collection ranked among the top 100 Golden Age comics in the Overstreet Comic Book Price Guide, a detail the Associated Press also cited in its coverage of the auction. That concentration of high-value issues is part of what convinced buyers and experts of the collection's authenticity.Comics from this era were printed on cheap, highly acidic wood-pulp newsprint, since publishers considered them disposable at the time. Research published in Polymer Degradation and Stability has shown that volatile organic compounds emitted by paper and archival materials continue to degrade them even in protective storage, which helps explain why so few Golden Age comics survive in good condition.As per AP (23 Feb., 2012) via Hurriyet Daily News, Heritage Auctions' sale of Billy Wright's Detective Comics #27 for nearly $523,000 is the highest selling price of this item in the New York auction of February 2012. In this regard, the first issue of Superman from the year 1938 called Action Comics No. 1 fetched a price of $298,750. Heritage Auctions (Feb. 2012) said Billy Wright’s copy of Batman #1 sold for $274,850 at the New York auction.The Antique Trader (February 18, 2025) reports that a Near Mint copy of Captain America Comics #2 (Timely, 1941) sold through Heritage Auctions for $113,500. This was close to the $113,525 that Wright's own copy of the same issue fetched at the original 2012 sale. A 2012 hedonic pricing study in the Journal of Cultural Economics , based on 1,100 American collectible comic books, found that a comic's condition, rarity, and documented ownership history each measurably affect its sale price, separate from the story or character inside; one reason collections with a clear, verified history like Wright's tend to command strong prices.Associated Press (Feb. 2012) stated that the Billy Wright comic book collection found by Michael Rorrer was auctioned off for around $3.5 million at Heritage Auctions' February 2012 auction, with the money split between Rorrer, his brother Jonathan, and his mother Lisa Hernandez. According to Lon Allen, the managing director of comic books at Heritage Auctions, this was a type of Golden Age comic book collection that everybody thought did not exist anymore.
Article Summary: Michael rorrer, a 31-year-old oxnard, california, resident, discovered 345 comics in a basement closet in his late great-aunt's martinsville, virginia, home in 2011. The collection was quietly assembled decades earlier by his great-uncle billy wright.

Article Title: Palantir, Nvidia curb AI model use, claims report
Article Text: Large technology companies, including Palantir Technologies, Nvidia and Booz Allen Hamilton, could restrict or cease to use advanced AI models unless Anthropic and OpenAI guarantee not to misuse their intellectual property, the Information reported on Monday.Anthropic faced customer pushback after a June policy change for its Fable model gave the company rights to retain usage logs for 30 days to guard against "complex and novel attacks," according to the report. OpenAI has faced similar scrutiny amid claims it may have trained models on user data to help solve a maths problem, the report said.Palantir has pressed Anthropic to provide irrevocable zero-data-retention guarantees before making its models available through Palantir's software, the report said. Nvidia limits Anthropic's use to less sensitive tasks and relies on its own Nemotron models for internal work, while Booz Allen has barred employees from using Anthropic's commercial model for cybersecurity work, the report said. Both AI labs say they do not train on customer data unless firms opt in, though they collect anonymised metadata to improve products, the report added.
Article Summary: Palantir technologies, nvidia and booz allen hamilton could restrict or cease to use advanced ai models. Anthropic and openai must guarantee not to misuse their intellectual property, report says. Both ai labs say they do not train on customer data unless firms opt in.
